prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

ISLAMABAD, Pakistan (CNN) -- Iran has condemned the kidnapping of one of its diplomats in northwest Pakistan on Thursday, calling it an "act of terrorism," an Iranian foreign ministry spokesman said. Pakistani policemen inspect a bullet-riddled car of a kidnapped Iranian diplomat on Thursday. "Pakistan should do its best to protect foreign diplomats and their residential places," the spokesman Hassan Qashqavi said, according to Iran's state-run IRNA news agency. At least four gunmen abducted Heshmatollah Attarzadeh near his home in Peshawar as he headed to work at the Iranian consulate, according to Pakistani police and Iranian diplomatic officials. His bodyguard, a Pakistani police officer, was shot and killed when the two men tried to resist, a Peshawar police official said. Pakistan's Foreign Minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi also "strongly condemned" the attack, and informed Iran that the government "will take all necessary measures for his safe and early recovery." Attarzadeh is a commercial attache for the Iranian consulate in Peshawar. It is the second attack targeting a foreign worker in Peshawar in two days. An American aid worker was shot and killed outside the Iranian consulate in Peshawar on Wednesday. Stephen Vance worked for a non-profit foundation funded by the U.S. Agency for International Development that helped find jobs for people in Pakistan's tribal regions, according to a statement from his employer, the Cooperative Housing Foundation International. "Stephen had fully immersed himself in the community in which he worked," the statement said. "He dressed traditionally and even sent his children to local schools." Vance, 52, a native of California, is survived by his wife and five children -- all of whom lived with him in Peshawar -- CHF International official Bill Holbrook told CNN. The attacks come less than three months after gunmen opened fire on a vehicle carrying the senior U.S. diplomat in Peshawar, Lynne Tracy. She escaped unharmed. Peshawar is the capital of Pakistan's North West Frontier Province, an area rife with Islamic extremists and the site of recent clashes between security forces and militants. In late June, Pakistan's military launched an offensive in the province -- the biggest push against extremists in the tribal region since the civilian government took power in March. Islamic militants vowed to retaliate. Since then, militants have launched several deadly attacks. Pakistan's new government has tried to negotiate a deal with militants as part of its efforts to bypass military might and achieve peace through talks.

Security analysts note that militant groups active in the border areas have periodically targeted foreigners, either for financial gain through ransom demands or to make political statements. The persistent instability has complicated diplomatic and commercial operations, prompting several countries to review security arrangements for their citizens working in Pakistan.

# Iranian Consulate Official Kidnapped in Peshawar; Guard Killed in Brazen Daylight Attack

**ISLAMABAD** — Gunmen ambushed and abducted a senior Iranian consulate official in the northwestern city of Peshawar on Thursday, killing his police guard in a brazen daylight assault that officials described as a "well-planned terrorist operation."

The official, identified as a commercial attaché at Iran's consulate in Peshawar, was seized as his vehicle traveled through the city's University Town district, an upscale neighborhood that houses several foreign missions and aid organizations.

"A group of armed men blocked the road and opened fire before dragging the official from his car," said a senior police official at the scene, speaking on condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to brief the media. "His guard resisted and was martyred. The attackers fled toward the outskirts within minutes."

Provincial Home Secretary confirmed the abduction, calling it "a cowardly act of terrorism aimed at destabilizing the region and damaging relations between two brotherly neighbors."

An Iranian Embassy spokesman in Islamabad said Tehran had lodged a formal protest and demanded the official's immediate and safe recovery. "We expect the Pakistani authorities to spare no effort in securing his release," the spokesman said. "The security of our diplomatic personnel is a matter of the highest concern."

No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack. Security analysts said the abduction bore the hallmarks of militant networks operating in the tribal belt straddling the border with Afghanistan, where kidnapping-for-ransom and hostage-taking of foreigners have become recurring tactics.

## A Volatile Frontier

The kidnapping is the latest in a wave of violence to grip Pakistan's North West Frontier Province, a strategically sensitive region that has borne the brunt of a spreading insurgency. The province, bordering the semi-autonomous tribal areas, has seen a sharp rise in suicide bombings, assassinations, and abductions targeting security forces, government officials, and foreigners.

Peshawar, the provincial capital, sits at the gateway to the Khyber Pass and has repeatedly been rocked by attacks as militancy spills out of the neighboring tribal agencies. In recent months, armed groups have grown increasingly bold, staging operations in the heart of the city despite a heavy security presence.

Foreign nationals have been frequent targets. Diplomats, aid workers, and businessmen have been kidnapped or killed in the frontier region, prompting several countries to restrict the movement of their personnel.

The targeting of an Iranian official adds a diplomatic dimension to the crisis. Iran shares a long, restive border with Pakistan to the south, and both nations have struggled to contain cross-border militancy.

## Search Underway

Security forces launched a manhunt across Peshawar and the surrounding districts, setting up checkpoints and conducting house-to-house searches on the city's outskirts, officials said. Roads leading toward the tribal areas were sealed in an effort to prevent the kidnappers from spiriting their captive across into ungoverned territory, where recovery becomes far more difficult.

"Our teams are pursuing all leads, and we are hopeful of a positive outcome," the police official said. "But the terrain and the network of these groups make such cases extremely challenging."

Federal authorities in Islamabad said they were coordinating with provincial officials and had assured the Iranian government of full cooperation.

*This is a developing story and will be updated as more information becomes available.*
